name: What is the right order for custom home planning steps?

mainEntity.name: What sequence should I follow when planning a custom home from land purchase to construction start?
mainEntity.text: What sequence should I follow when planning a custom home from land purchase to construction start?

acceptedAnswer.text: A custom home is easier to manage when the planning steps happen in the right order. The process usually starts with feasibility review and budget alignment, followed by site due diligence such as survey and soils work. From there, the team develops the concept design, then schematic and permit-ready drawings with architectural, structural, civil, and energy coordination as needed. After submittal, the project may go through correction cycles before permit issuance and construction start. Skipping or compressing these steps usually creates problems later because the design may not fit the site, the budget may be unrealistic, or the permit set may be incomplete. Homeowners in Los Angeles should give extra attention to early site analysis because zoning, grading, and neighborhood conditions can affect the entire sequence. A clear roadmap at the beginning saves both time and money.
acceptedAnswer.description: The usual order is feasibility review, design concept, survey and soils work, schematic plans, engineering, permit drawings, permit submittal, corrections, and then construction. Skipping steps often leads to redesign and delays. The earlier the site and budget are validated, the easier it is to keep the project on track.
